incidente.resumo: A configuration change on a backbone router in Atlanta contained an error that caused all traffic across Cloudflare's backbone to be sent to Atlanta, overwhelming the Atlanta router and causing backbone-connected network locations to fail; the outage lasted 27 minutes and traffic dropped by about 50%. Service was restored after the Atlanta router was disabled.
servicos_afetados: Cloudflare network locations connected to the backbone

descricao.texto: To remove some of Atlanta's backbone traffic, a one-line change was made on the Atlanta router that deactivated the prefix-list condition of the 6-SITE-LOCAL term instead of the term itself. Without the prefix-list condition, the router sent all its BGP routes to all other backbone routers with an increased local-preference of 200, and Atlanta started attracting traffic from across the backbone, which overwhelmed the Atlanta router and caused backbone-connected locations to fail.
trechos: As there was backbone congestion in Atlanta, the team had decided to remove some of Atlanta’s backbone traffic. But instead of removing the Atlanta routes from the backbone, a one line change started leaking all BGP routes into the backbone.
The correct change would have been to deactivate the term instead of the prefix-list.
By removing the prefix-list condition, the router was instructed to send all its BGP routes to all other backbone routers, with an increased local-preference of 200.
With the routes sent out, Atlanta started attracting traffic from across the backbone.
This quickly overwhelmed the Atlanta router and caused Cloudflare network locations connected to the backbone to fail.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: At the time, local routes that the edge routers received from compute nodes had a local-preference of 100, lower than the 200 set by the leaked routes; as the higher local-preference wins, traffic meant for local compute nodes went to Atlanta compute nodes instead.
trechos: Unfortunately at the time, local routes that the edge routers received from our compute nodes had a local-preference of 100. As the higher local-preference wins, all of the traffic meant for local compute nodes went to Atlanta compute nodes instead.

descricao.texto: A one-line change on the Atlanta router (atl01) deactivated the prefix-list 6-SITE-LOCAL in term 6-SITE-LOCAL of policy-statement 6-BBONE-OUT.
trechos: But instead of removing the Atlanta routes from the backbone, a one line change started leaking all BGP routes into the backbone.

passos.texto: Once the outage was understood, the Atlanta router was disabled and dropped from the backbone; traffic began flowing normally again at 21:39 UTC, and the timeline marks 21:39 to 21:47 as ATL dropped from the backbone, service restored.
trechos: Once the outage was understood, the Atlanta router was disabled and traffic began flowing normally again at 21:39.
21:39 to 21:47: ATL dropped from the backbone, service restored

acoes.texto: Already done: the BGP local-preference for local server routes was changed after the incident, to prevent a single location from attracting other locations' traffic in a similar manner.
trechos: Change the BGP local-preference for local server routes. This change will prevent a single location from attracting other locations’ traffic in a similar manner. This change has been deployed following the incident.

acoes.texto: Planned: introduce a maximum-prefix limit on backbone BGP sessions, to be deployed on Monday, July 20; the authors say this would have shut down the backbone in Atlanta, and the network is built to function without a backbone.
trechos: Introduce a maximum-prefix limit on our backbone BGP sessions - this would have shut down the backbone in Atlanta, but our network is built to function properly without a backbone. This change will be deployed on Monday, July 20.
Today a configuration error in our backbone network caused an outage for Internet properties and Cloudflare services that lasted 27 minutes.

observacoes: The text gives no full date for the incident (only "Today" and a planned deployment on "Monday, July 20" without a year), so data_incidente is null. After the outage, congestion at a core data center caused some logs to be dropped from 21:47 to 22:10 UTC while the edge continued operating; full recovery including logs and metrics was at 22:10. categoria_causa is configuration-error because the text presents the root cause as an erroneous policy change ("a configuration error"). The text states this was not caused by an attack or breach.
